Agree with the 'get gud' message, but life is definitely long enough to master various things.

The 10,000 hour rule isn't precise, and it doesn't overcome natural abilities as studies have shown - but the underlying principle that a ton of focused practice will make you good at something still holds. If you do 10,000 hours of creating and trying stand-up comedy, then making new bits, then adjusting old ones, then you might not be the next Louis CK, but you'll definitely be a comic. If you study and play and study chess for 10,000 hours, you probably won't be the next Magnus Carlsen, but you'll definitely be a chess player.

The great thing is that 10,000 hours can be done multiple times in your life. If you can do something for 14 hours a week (that's an hour a day for 6 days and 8 hours on your day off from work), then you can be really, really good at that thing in 14 years with a bit of time to spare. If you decide, today, that you want to be something, you can be that person 14-15 years from now. The thing is: most people quit. Most people can't keep trying at something for 5 years and not achieve that dream and still keep pouring tons of energy into it. It's all about that discipline.
